subject: Disability Fair and Accessibility Planning
overview: The commission opened its 2025–2026 cycle to plan the annual Disability Fair, review park and school accessibility upgrades, and discuss efforts to improve accessible voting options and public library access.

items.title: Introductions and Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Commissioners introduced themselves and approved the meeting minutes from June 2025.

items.title: Open Meeting Law Review
items.summary: Frances Nwajei reviewed Open Meeting Law compliance guidelines, emphasizing transparency and the avoidance of accidental quorums outside of official sessions.

items.title: Meeting Calendar Adjustment
items.summary: Approved combining the November and December meetings into a single session on December 10, 2025.

items.title: Community Access Monitoring Training
items.summary: Frances Nwajei announced upcoming virtual Community Access Monitoring training opportunities hosted by the Massachusetts Office on Disability.

items.title: Disability Specialist Update
items.summary: Nicholas Karinge reported on new commissioner stipends, upcoming ADA-compliant renovations for City Hall restrooms, completed ramp work at the McGlynn School, and online instructions for accessing school Gaga pits.

items.title: Disability Fair Scheduling
items.summary: Commissioners discussed potential dates in May 2026 to schedule the annual Disability Fair without holiday conflicts.

items.title: Commission Project Planning
items.summary: Commissioners discussed goals for the upcoming year, including reviewing the city's accessibility ordinance, improving inter-commission communication, and organizing a field trip to audit the public library's accessibility.

items.title: Open Space and Recreation Plan Update
items.summary: Amanda Centrella presented community survey feedback on park accessibility barriers to inform the Open Space and Recreation Plan extension, and she invited the commission to a COVID Memorial Grove workshop.

items.title: Accessible Voting and Elections Update
items.summary: Frances Nwajei read a statement from the elections department regarding voting machine calibration and testing, prompting a discussion on poll worker training and alternative voting methods.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: A resident suggested the commission explore a policy to redirect handicap parking violation fines directly to the commission's budget, similar to an initiative in Somerville.
